knowledge.statement: When a candidate becomes leader it adopts two independently ordered inputs in one call: the log comes from the promise that is strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx) with pid only as tiebreak, while the decided index is the maximum decided index over all recorded promises; sync_log then writes that decided index and the adopted log in the same storage transaction, and the leader path contains no clamp comparing the two.

interpretations.rationale: Source trace only, no execution. handle_majority_promises pairs two independently ordered inputs: the log_sync of the promise that is strictly greatest under (n_accepted, accepted_idx) (set_promise only replaces max_promise_meta on a strict Greater, and PromiseMetaData's ordering ignores decided_idx) and the maximum decided_idx across all recorded promises (get_max_decided_idx). sync_log then stores the adopted decided index together with the adopted log and does not clamp. Because the decided index adopted is a different node's report, a history in which the greatest-accepted promise holds fewer entries than another promise's reported decided index would leave the new leader reporting a decided index beyond the entries it holds; every observed run so far has the two orders coincide (the greatest-accepted promise was also the greatest decided reporter), so no witness exists. The suspicion is therefore unresolved rather than refuted: the reachability argument I can give (a decided entry must be accepted by a write quorum that intersects every read quorum, so the greatest-accepted promise should cover it) is exactly the protocol invariant that this code relies on instead of a local bound, and I have not turned it into a reachable disagreement history.
limitations: No execution: the child question rests on reading handle_majority_promises, set_promise and get_max_decided_idx, not on an observed disagreement.

The orderings only differ when the promise with the greatest (n_accepted, accepted_idx) is not the promise with the greatest decided_idx; constructing such a history within the protocol's own constraints was not achieved in this turn.

The already-witnessed inflation produces an accepted index above the replica's content but left the adopted decided index at or below the leader's accepted index in the newterm and staleleader stages, so it does not serve as a witness for this question.

investigations.discriminator: A history in which the promise with the greatest accepted round and index is not the promise with the greatest decided index, so that the newly elected leader's adopted decided index exceeds the entries the adopted log provides; the decisive observation is the new leader's decided index against its accepted index and its readable decided log immediately after its prepare phase.
